title: A Count Depends On Its Method

scenes.tts: Four careful censuses of mouse retinal ganglion cells gave at least thirty two, at least thirty five, forty two, and forty six. Each was done well. Yet the numbers disagree. Ganglion cell axons form the optic nerve. So how many kinds are there, and who is right?
scenes.caption: Four careful censuses of mouse retinal ganglion cells gave at least 32, at least 35, 42, and 46. Each was done well. Yet the numbers disagree. Ganglion cell axons form the optic nerve. So how many kinds are there, and who is right?
scenes.visual: Four count chips appear one by one over a ganglion cell whose axon joins the optic nerve; a question mark grows between them.
scenes.narration: Four careful censuses of mouse retinal ganglion cells gave at least 32, at least 35, 42, and 46. Each was done well. Yet the numbers disagree. Ganglion cell axons form the optic nerve. So how many kinds are there, and who is right?

scenes.tts: Imaging counted cells by their light responses. In isolated mouse retina, two photon imaging built a data set of eleven thousand two hundred ten cells. But that layer also holds displaced amacrine cells. Fourteen groups of them were set aside. What remained was a minimum of thirty two types. The authors thought unusually abundant types probably hide further subdivisions.

scenes.visual: A layer of dots flashes yellow; displaced amacrine dots turn red and are removed; a bar of 32 grows with a dashed open top.

scenes.tts: Sequencing counted cells by which genes they express. In adult mice, thirty five thousand six hundred ninety nine ganglion cell transcriptomes fell into forty five clusters. Subdividing one cluster gave forty six types. So the count depends on how finely the data are split. The smallest type was zero point one five percent of the cells. That is about fifty four cells.
scenes.caption: Sequencing counted cells by which genes they express. In adult mice, 35,699 ganglion cell transcriptomes fell into 45 clusters. Subdividing one cluster gave 46 types. So the count depends on how finely the data are split. The smallest type was 0.15% of the cells. That is about 54 cells.

scenes.tts: Recording from the same cell ties response, shape, and RNA to that one cell. In some cells, the shape or the RNA was collected too. In isolated mouse retina, one thousand eight hundred fifty nine ganglion cells were recorded and sorted into forty two functional types. These were estimated to cover eighty nine percent of the population. But the map to RNA was not always one to one. Three sustained O N direction selective types aligned with a single cluster, called C ten.
scenes.caption: Recording from the same cell ties response, shape, and RNA to that one cell. In some cells, the shape or the RNA was collected too. In isolated mouse retina, 1,859 ganglion cells were recorded and sorted into 42 functional types. These were estimated to cover 89% of the population. But the map to RNA was not always one to one. Three sustained ON direction-selective types aligned with a single cluster, called C10.

scenes.tts: Electron microscopy counted by shape. In one mouse retinal patch, the reconstructed cells formed forty seven anatomical clusters. The supported lower bound was thirty five types. Forty seven counts clusters. Thirty five is the number they could support. So the four numbers are not rival answers to one question. Each reflects a method, a preparation, and a resolution.

scenes.tts: So when does a cluster become a type? When response, shape, and expression are tied to one another. The usual standard also asks for a mosaic. Cells of the type space themselves, so their dendrites tile the retina. Ideally, genetic access agrees too. The most trustworthy types are the ones that more than one method finds. Ask what a number counted.
